Review this card after **Pipeline tuning**. Completed trial results flow downstream
without accepting a model in the tuning card. This card compares configurations
within each method and trade-offs between model methods. It performs no model
fitting and constructs no ensemble.

### Within a method

Choose a method on the front and **Within method** in settings. Each point is a
shortlisted configuration's mean primary-metric loss relative to that method's
best-scoring trial. Positive loss means worse performance, for both minimizing
and maximizing metrics. The reference is explicitly identified; it has no
self-comparison probability. There are no uncertainty bars.

Set **Practical-equivalence tolerance** in primary-metric units based on application
needs, ideally before reviewing results. The shaded region marks plus/minus this
tolerance. Green points meet the **Comparison decision probability** for practical
equivalence; red points meet it for meaningful inferiority. Gray points are
inconclusive. A missing or inconclusive comparison is not evidence of equivalence.
Points also show the probability of lying within tolerance when estimable.

Comparisons use the same paired, dependence-corrected Student-t Bayesian approach
as the [sklearn example](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/model_selection/plot_grid_search_stats.html#pairwise-comparison-of-all-models-bayesian-approach).
They require upstream repeated shuffled ordinary or stratified K-fold CV and
matching complete split identities. Other resampling designs still show scores
and diagnostics, with comparisons labeled inconclusive. Shortlisting and selecting
the reference on these same results leaves selection bias: these are exploratory
comparisons, not an independent confirmation of generalization performance.
Equivalence is relative to a method's best, not between every shortlisted pair.

The card shows only short status messages. A blank equivalence tolerance leaves
paired assessments inconclusive; choose an application-based tolerance to enable
them. No automatic acceptance, complexity ranking or ensemble construction is
performed. Interpretability descriptions are qualitative and do not establish
causal effects, including when a Treatment role is present.

On the flip side, **Selected configuration and parameter differences** opens when
a trial is selected and closes when the selection is cleared. Compare two trials
from the same method. Best-score reference rows use emphasized text. **Download**
saves the candidate comparison as CSV. Parameter labels use the method name and
a readable path: for example, `cand_methods__estimator__depth` appears as
**Cat Boost: estimator-depth** for Cat Boost Regressor trials. These are display
labels; the underlying pipeline keys and saved parameter values are unchanged.
The parameter column wraps long labels so the full name remains visible.

**Top trials per method** limits each method separately, so one method cannot
crowd out the others. Select a point or flip-side row to inspect the configuration.
Choose another configuration of the same method in **Compare selected configuration with**.
The parameter-difference table shows only settings that differ between the pair. Original unfitted pipelines supply effective
values, including settings omitted from an inactive conditional trial branch.

### Between methods

Choose **Between methods**. One representative per method appears in a scatter
plot, initially its best-scoring shortlisted trial. To choose another, select its
row and click **Use selected as representative**. This does not accept a pipeline.
Select axes from Score, error risk and Observed rows/s. Method names appear in the
full-screen legend and hover text. Points on the Pareto frontier use diamonds:
no other displayed representative is better in both chosen criteria. Missing
measurements receive no frontier status. This is a comparison on those two axes,
not an overall recommendation or a weighted score.

For regression, **P95 absolute error** is the mean of the 95th percentile of
held-out absolute errors calculated separately for each CV repeat. It describes
large-error behavior in response units. It is not a prediction interval.

For classification, **Error rate** describes incorrect labels and **Log loss**
assesses predicted probabilities where supported. Class labels are never
subtracted as though they were numerical regression outcomes. Positive probability
losses are averaged within repeats, then across repeats.

**Observed rows/s** divides held-out row count by the total time for an additional
warm `predict` call on each validation batch. It includes upstream transforms,
uses tuning's thread limits, and can be affected by concurrent workers, batch size
and host load. It measures label/point prediction, not probability generation.
It is diagnostic timing, not a standardized production-throughput benchmark.

Interpretability descriptions are qualitative reasons, not numerical complexity
scores or guarantees. A Treatment role draws attention to explanation needs;
predictive accuracy and an interpretable model do not establish causal treatment
effects. Use domain requirements alongside these views.

### Error exceedance

**Error exceedance** shows the percentage of held-out observations whose error
exceeds each threshold. For regression this uses absolute error. For classification
it uses log loss if all selected representatives have probability evidence;
otherwise all use 0/1 classification errors so unlike quantities are not mixed.
Each curve is calculated per repeat and then averaged. Repeated predictions for
one observation are not treated as independent additional subjects.

### Accepting a configuration

Select a completed candidate row or point and click **Accept selected model**.
The output carries its full unfitted pipeline and preserves the evaluation
evidence. No final fitting or holdout evaluation occurs. **Revert acceptance**
passes through the incoming selection. Representative choices and acceptance
persist with card configuration only for the same search fingerprint.

Tuning retains fold scores, parameter choices, prediction timing and compact error
summaries. It does **not** retain row-level predictions, outcomes, positions or
class-probability matrices. Exact repeat-wise P95 and the displayed 101-point
exceedance curves are computed before temporary validation-loss arrays are
deleted. Shared data, resampling and one unfitted template per method are retained
once; trial pipelines are constructed only when needed.

Completed configurations are self-contained JSON and require no evidence files.
For a paused trial only, its unfinished compressed loss arrays are embedded in
saved checkpoints/configurations and restored into a fresh isolated cache. They
are verified by checksum and tied to the correct trial/split; host paths are not
saved. Browser restoration uses compressed bytes rather than native files.
Large configuration reloads use IndexedDB instead of the small sessionStorage
quota. Completed archives can be reviewed read-only when the source-data and
preprocessing signature match but the original native fitting environment or
search settings are unavailable. Pipeline acceptance stays disabled until a
matching native search environment is restored; unavailable model classes do not
prevent review of their saved scores and compact error summaries. Temporary arrays are removed on trial completion/failure, reset or session
cleanup. The native cache itself is temporary and disappears at process exit.

Historical row-level evidence is discarded on import while score history is
preserved. Start a new search to collect compact diagnostics under the current
implementation. Changed source data, roles, resampling or preprocessing invalidate
inherited evidence. Failed/incomplete trials are not review candidates. Future
ensemble residual analysis will need to regenerate row-level predictions for its
selected models; they are not kept speculatively by this card.

Ensembling is reserved for a later downstream card. This card does not compute or
aggregate model complexity.
